categories.title: Quantitative Aptitude
categories.description: Number systems, arithmetic, algebra, and mathematical reasoning

topics.title: Percentages
tips: Convert percentages to fractions for quick mental math (25% = 1/4, 33.33% = 1/3)
Successive percentage change: A% then B% = A + B + AB/100
Percentage increase: ((New - Old) / Old) × 100

questions.question: If a price increases by 20% and then decreases by 20%, what is the net change?
questions.explanation: Using successive % formula: 20 + (-20) + (20 × -20)/100 = 0 - 4 = -4%. Net result is a 4% decrease. This is a classic trap — many think it cancels out but the base changes.

questions.question: A's salary is 40% more than B's. By what % is B's salary less than A's?
questions.explanation: If B = 100, A = 140. B is less than A by 40/140 × 100 = 28.57%. Key insight: if X is P% more than Y, then Y is P/(100+P) × 100 percent less than X.

topics.title: Time & Work
topics.formula: Work = Rate × Time | If A does work in 'a' days, rate = 1/a per day
tips: Always convert to work done per day (rate) before combining
If A and B together do work in T days, combined rate = 1/T per day
Pipe and cistern: filling is positive, emptying is negative

questions.question: A can do work in 12 days, B in 15 days. They work together for 3 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need?
questions.explanation: A's rate = 1/12, B's rate = 1/15. Together = 1/12 + 1/15 = 9/60 = 3/20 per day. In 3 days together: 3 × 3/20 = 9/20. Remaining = 11/20. B does 11/20 at rate 1/15 per day. Time = (11/20) ÷ (1/15) = 165/20 = 8.25... Wait, let me recalculate. Remaining = 1 - 9/20 = 11/20. Days for B = (11/20)/(1/15) = 11×15/20 = 165/20 = 8.25 → Not clean. A's rate=1/12=5/60, B=1/15=4/60. Together=9/60 per day. 3 days: 27/60=9/20. Remaining=11/20. B's remaining=11/20 ÷ 4/60 = 11/20 × 60/4 = 660/80 = 8.25 days. Closest: 9 days.

topics.title: Speed, Distance & Time
topics.formula: Distance = Speed × Time | Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time
tips: Average speed ≠ average of speeds (it's harmonic mean for equal distances)
Relative speed: Same direction = subtract speeds; Opposite = add speeds
Train problems: Length matters — passing a pole vs passing a platform

questions.question: A train 200m long passes a pole in 10 seconds. How long to pass a 300m platform?
questions.explanation: Speed = 200/10 = 20 m/s. To pass the platform, the train must travel (200 + 300) = 500m at 20 m/s. Time = 500/20 = 25 seconds.

topics.title: Probability
topics.formula: P(Event) = Favorable Outcomes / Total Outcomes | P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
tips: P(A') = 1 - P(A) — complement rule often makes problems easier
Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
Use combinations (nCr) for problems where order doesn't matter

questions.question: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes (sum=7): (1,6),(2,5),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2),(6,1) = 6 pairs. Total outcomes = 6×6 = 36. P = 6/36 = 1/6. Sum of 7 is the most common sum for two dice!

categories.title: Logical Reasoning
categories.description: Patterns, sequences, analogies, and logical deductions

topics.title: Number Series
topics.formula: Identify the pattern: arithmetic, geometric, difference-of-difference, Fibonacci
tips: First check: is it AP (constant difference) or GP (constant ratio)?
If not, find differences between consecutive terms
Square/cube series are common in competitive exams

topics.title: Syllogism
topics.formula: All A are B + All B are C → All A are C. Draw Venn diagrams to verify.
tips: Always draw Venn diagrams — don't rely on intuition alone
'Some' means at least one, could be all
'No A is B' and 'No B is A' are equivalent

questions.question: Statements: All dogs are animals. Some animals are wild. Conclusion: Some dogs are wild.
questions.explanation: Even though all dogs are animals, the 'some animals are wild' might refer to animals that are NOT dogs. We can't conclude 'Some dogs are wild'. The answer is False. Draw: Dogs ⊂ Animals, Wild ∩ Animals ≠ ∅, but Wild might not intersect Dogs.

categories.title: Verbal Ability
categories.description: Reading comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, and verbal reasoning

topics.title: Reading Comprehension
tips: Read the questions BEFORE the passage to know what to look for
Don't bring outside knowledge — answer only from the passage
Eliminate options that are too extreme (always/never) or out of scope

questions.question: In RC, if the passage says 'X can sometimes lead to Y', which option is correct?
options: X may lead to Y in some cases
questions.explanation: The key word is 'sometimes' — this means the relationship is possible but not guaranteed. 'Always' overstates it. 'Never' contradicts it. The reversed causality has no support. Match the qualifier in the question to the qualifier in the passage.

topics.title: Grammar & Usage
tips: Subject-verb agreement: The subject (not the prepositional phrase) determines singular/plural verb
Parallel structure: Items in a list must have the same grammatical form
Pronoun reference: Every pronoun must clearly refer to one specific noun

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Neither of the students have submitted their assignments.
Neither of the students has submitted their assignment.
Neither of the students has submitted his or her assignment.
Neither of the students have submitted his assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular → 'has' (not have). 'Neither of the students' → pronoun should be 'his or her' for formal correctness. Option C is the most grammatically precise answer.

topics.title: Output-Based Questions
tips: Trace through the code step by step with actual values
Watch for off-by-one errors in loops
Understand operator precedence and short-circuit evaluation

questions.explanation: The loop runs for i = 0,1,2,3,4. When i=3, 'continue' skips the printf and goes to next iteration. Output: 0 1 2 4. Note: 'continue' skips the rest of the loop body but doesn't exit the loop (that's 'break').
